summary: Multiplies a 3x3 matrix (nine floats at this, offsets 0x0..0x20) by a three-component vector a2 and stores the result in a3. Three output components are each a dot product of one matrix row with the input vector. Returns the original input vector pointer a2. Pure math utility used for rigid-body transforms; called by VehicleGeometryProximityTest and RayTriangleIntersectionWithBarycentricCoordinate.

operations.description: result = a2, so the caller receives back the input vector pointer.
a3[0] = this[0]*a2[0] + this[1]*a2[1] + this[2]*a2[2]: row 0 of the matrix (this+0x0, this+0x4, this+0x8) dotted with a2.
a3[1] = this[3]*a2[0] + this[4]*a2[1] + this[5]*a2[2]: row 1 of the matrix (this+0xC, this+0x10, this+0x14) dotted with a2.
a3[2] = this[6]*a2[0] + this[7]*a2[1] + this[8]*a2[2]: row 2 of the matrix (this+0x18, this+0x1C, this+0x20) dotted with a2.
Return result, which is the unmodified a2 pointer.

unresolved: Row-major matrix layout is inferred from the index pattern; the actual storage order of the caller's 3x3 transform is not proven.
Whether the 3x3 matrix is an orientation-only rotation or an upper-left sub-block of a 4x4 transform depends on the callers.
